target.title: fix(qqbot): require own account credential entries
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where QQBot logout/setup credential cleanup could treat prototype-inherited named account entries or inherited credential fields as explicit user config. In affected programmatic config shapes, logout could report cleanup for config the user did not own or continue resolving inherited credentials after cleanup skipped the write.

## Why This Change Was Made

QQBot credential cleanup now uses own-property checks across the complete logout/setup account path. Named account resolution, default-account selection, setup updates, bridge resolution, and credential clearing agree that only own `channels.qqbot.accounts.<id>` entries and own `clientSecret` / `clientSecretFile` fields are mutable user config.

Named account objects are normalized to their own enumerable properties before engine and bridge credential resolution, so an owned account entry cannot inherit `appId`, `clientSecret`, or `clientSecretFile` from its prototype.

## User Impact

QQBot logout and setup cleanup now ignore prototype-inherited account data and clear only credentials actually present on the user's config object. Normal owned-account logout still removes `clientSecret` / `clientSecretFile`, retains non-secret fields such as `appId`, and writes the cleaned config through the existing runtime path.

Programmatic configurations that intentionally depend on prototype-inherited QQBot properties will no longer resolve those properties. JSON/JSON5 config files cannot encode prototype inheritance.

## Evidence

Exact head: `a69ebffb631dd1227defdca84a50e8508a3f2a81`

Current-main refresh:

- Rebasing the six commits from base `9043bcf230a008301edd9abf62068075f55a08cf` onto main `2808507c3be51203eded54deffc37ddd9eceea36` completed without conflicts.
- `git range-diff` mapped all six commits with `=`; old-head and new-head content for all six PR files is identical.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- Exact-head upstream CI: [run 29416389756](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29416389756), 86 completed checks, zero failures.

Exact-head inherited-object proof:

- Secretless fork workflow: [run 29416680965](https://github.com/Alix-007/openclaw/actions/runs/29416680965), Ubuntu 24.04, Node 24.15.0.
- The workflow explicitly checked out and verified `a69ebffb631dd1227defdca84a50e8508a3f2a81`.
- It constructed an owned named account with `Object.create`-inherited `appId`, `clientSecret`, and `clientSecretFile`, then exercised production `resolveAccountBase`, the public channel plugin resolver, and gateway `logoutAccount`.
- No credential values were printed or read.

Redacted output:

```text
head=a69ebffb631dd1227defdca84a50e8508a3f2a81
inputOwnKeys=["enabled","name"]
base.appIdLength=0
base.enabled=false
base.configKeys=["enabled","name"]
plugin.appIdLength=0
plugin.secretLength=0
plugin.secretSource=none
plugin.configKeys=["enabled","name"]
logout={"ok":true,"cleared":false,"envToken":false,"loggedOut":true}
all_inherited_config_checks=true
PROOF_RESULT=PASS
```

Focused exact-head validation from the same run:

```text
Test Files  3 passed (3)
Tests       19 passed (19)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard
No extension plugin-sdk boundary violations found.
Baseline matches (0 entries).
```

The focused tests cover inherited named entries, inherited credential fields on owned entries, normal owned credential cleanup, resolver behavior, and gateway logout behavior.

Not tested:

- No live QQBot API request, gateway connection, or real credential was used.
- This ran from the source checkout rather than an npm-installed QQBot package.
